nodes.label: FlatAim KPF Tar-Format Mount Failure
nodes.rationale: F5 was assumed blocked by hotkey/DLL/load-order problems; the KPF package was actually tar-format while working mods are ZIP/PK, so KEX could not mount kpf:/mods/flataim/ paths (path not found). Repacking as ZIP/PK fixed the Squirrel bridge load.

nodes.label: FlatAim KexSetConfigRaw Hook Crash Misdiagnosis
nodes.rationale: Wrong theory: the installed KexSetConfigRaw config-setter detour was suspected as the cause of a save-load crash at RVA 0x8D4700. Disabling the hook entirely (config_hook=0, then block_without_bridge=1) did not stop the crash, falsifying the config hook as direct cause.

nodes.label: Contaminated Debug-View Save Crash Root Cause
nodes.rationale: Root cause found after the config-hook theory was falsified: the crashing 'Flataim' save was created during an earlier FlatAim build while debug_view_enabled was active, persisting bad debug-view/cursor-mode/list state. A fresh save created after leaving debug view loaded successfully, confirming the old save was a contaminated-state artifact rather than a live bug.

nodes.label: Native Cursor Globals Crosshair-Driver Misdiagnosis
nodes.rationale: Wrong theory: writing the FlatAim internal cursor pixel into KEX native cursor globals DAT_1413179b8/938 was expected to move the visible stock crosshair. Readback moved but the visible crosshair stayed centered, falsifying the native cursor globals as the crosshair's actual driver; work pivoted to a ShockOverlay-drawn replacement reticle (kOverlayCrosshair=22).

nodes.label: ShockOverlay Reticle Origin-Bias Fix
nodes.rationale: The replacement ShockOverlay reticle appeared offset right/down from the DLL-published center aim. Root cause was a ShockOverlay draw-origin/safe-area bias; v0.9 fixed it by subtracting hudCanvas/16 (about 60x33.75 HUD px) before DrawBitmap.

nodes.label: FlatAim Stale Startup Aim Clear Fix
nodes.rationale: After the origin-bias fix, the normal gameplay crosshair appeared offset on load before F5 was even pressed. Root cause: stale valid ss2fa_aim state survived from a previous run into script load/startup. Fixed by clearing ss2fa_aim on script load and publishing an invalid startup aim from the DLL.

nodes.label: FlatAim Visible Weapon Pitch-Dependent Roll Bug
nodes.rationale: Recurring symptom across a dozen-plus builds (v0.11-v0.28): horizontal mouse aim visually turns into weapon roll as camera pitch rises, with roll direction flipping above/below horizon. Root cause was ultimately a heading-axis-convention mismatch, not a sign/offset problem.

nodes.label: CameraObj Euler Scalar Roll-Compensation Misdiagnosis (Modes 1-6)
nodes.rationale: Wrong theory pursued across weapon_follow_mode 1 through 6: that scalar Heading/Pitch/Bank formula tuning and sign flips on the final native CameraObj representation could fix the pitch-dependent roll. Every variant (cos/sin compensation, bank cancellation, rig-level aimPoint insertion, screen-axis variants) was falsified by live retest; the user explicitly challenged whether the team understood the issue or was 'layering band-aids.'

nodes.label: FlatAim World-Space Weapon Proxy (Mode 7)
nodes.rationale: After scalar CameraObj tuning was abandoned, v0.20 introduced a transient world-space object cloned from the weapon model, hidden the native viewmodel, and positioned/faced independently via Object.Teleport. Multiple facing-decomposition sub-attempts (facingMode 0/1/4/5/6/7) still rolled until the true Dark heading convention was found.

nodes.label: Dark Heading-Axis Convention Root Cause Fix
nodes.rationale: Root cause: Dark's matrix inverse reads world-object heading as atan2(forward.y, forward.x), while FlatAim's proxy heading computation used atan2(dir.x, dir.y) -- a swapped-argument convention mismatch, not a sign or scalar-tuning problem. Mode 8 rebuilt an upright Dark basis (forward/right/up) and extracted heading/pitch/bank using the correct atan2 argument order.

nodes.label: FlatAim Ray-Cylinder Object Selector Misdiagnosis
nodes.rationale: Wrong approach: the original selector scored candidate objects by origin-distance to a 3D ray cylinder, so clustered floor pistols with similar origin-to-ray distances could hop or win selection from surprising screen positions, unlike inventory-mode cursor picking.

nodes.label: FlatAim Screen-Projected Semantic Selection (Mode 2)
nodes.rationale: Fix for the ray-cylinder misdiagnosis: selection_semantic_mode=2 projects candidate objects with ShockOverlay.WorldToScreen and compares them to the actual drawn reticle point, matching inventory-style cursor picking. User confirmed it 'solved the selection issue in one pass.'

nodes.label: FlatAim Native-Looking Bracket Marker (BRACK0-3)
nodes.rationale: Draws stock BRACK0-3 ShockOverlay bitmaps around the screen-projected semantic target as a substitute for the still-uninvestigated true native bracket path; user reported the visuals were 'WAY better.'

nodes.label: FlatAim Laser Bolt Rotation Reflection Misdiagnosis
nodes.rationale: First patch attempt treated the rotated (horizontal blue line) Laser Pistol bolt as a reflection-style visual-orientation bug and was wrong. The actual cause was the same heading-axis-convention issue as the weapon roll bug: FlatAim aim heading used atan2(x,y) from +Y while KEX object facing needed atan2(y,x) from +X.

nodes.label: FlatAim Long-Weapon Proxy Pivot Fix
nodes.rationale: Long weapons rotated around the short-gun/pistol origin so their butt swung into view at low-right aim. Fixed as a proxy pivot/model-origin placement problem (weapon_proxy_pivot_long_forward/left/up), explicitly not a reticle/projectile/facing math fix.

nodes.label: FlatAim Melee Viewmodel Spin/Orbit Bug
nodes.rationale: Root cause: native NDShockMeleeViewmodel.OnFrameUpdate() only writes PlyrArm Location, never Heading/Pitch/Bank; FlatAim's orientation writes to those fields were therefore fighting/compounding with native state and caused the Wrench to spin rapidly around the player on left/right aim. Fixed by making mode 3 write no facing fields (writeFacing=0) and using camera-screen-plane location offset only.

nodes.label: FlatAim F5 Blocked by Squirrel Syntax Error
nodes.rationale: F5 doing nothing looked like the recurring Squirrel-bridge-missing symptom, but condump.txt showed the real cause was a Squirrel compile error (extra closing parenthesis in an [SS2FA-MELEE] pose diagnostic print) that prevented ss2fa.nut from loading at all.

nodes.label: Viewmodel World-Depth Occlusion Spike (Phase 4.2.2)
nodes.rationale: D3D11 hook remembers non-backbuffer scene color/depth at draw time, arms on a pointer-matched depth clear, then preserves/binds that depth around the viewmodel DrawIndexed cluster so nearby world geometry occludes the weapon. Confirmed live in headset: 'YES! Depth occlusion is WORKING!!' Kept default-off pending a broader multi-weapon regression sweep.

nodes.label: Existing-Save Patcher Root-Object Shape Fix
nodes.rationale: The offline save patcher's root-object guard rejected a smaller/different save (header_size=0xF8, root length 0x24) with 'unexpected root table/vtable shape' even though the needed title/level/mods fields existed. Relaxed the guard to accept shorter root objects when those specific fields exist and fit.

nodes.label: Left-Hand Additive Viewmodel Shaded-Material White/Purple Bug
nodes.rationale: Long A/B probe saga: the additive standalone left-hand model rendered bright self-illuminated white (or purple/black with a red-material probe) under every shaded material variant tried (custom opaque material, copied ND-arm.dds, $TEXTURE, explicit local paths), while the same texture/mesh rendered correctly under an unshaded (shaded 0) pass. Isolated the bug to the shaded/lit render path specifically, not texture lookup or model geometry.

nodes.label: Left-Hand Material Include-Chain Packaging Root Cause
nodes.rationale: Root cause: the custom package .mtl included ../../materials/ND-hand.inc, but that include chain was never packaged inside the SS2VR KPF. Stock ND-arm.mtl resolves its ../../materials/ND-viewmodel.inc include from the base sshock2ee package, but custom package-local materials resolve relative to their own KPF and crash/fail when the include is missing. Fixed in KPF v1.49 by packaging ND-pass_dif/fill/rim.inc and ND-IR_rim.png locally.

nodes.label: Jointed Standalone LGMD Root-Subobject Crash
nodes.rationale: Preserving source joint metadata (motion_type=2,joint_id=2) on a one-subobject standalone hand extract crashed AE with a null-pointer access violation at .text:1408F8B6B, because in the known-good model that subobject is a jointed child in a full hierarchy, not a root. Falsified 'preserve source joint metadata' for standalone single-subobject extracts; the exporter now rejects that combination. Static-metadata rebuild alone still crashed until the include-chain root cause was also fixed.

nodes.label: RenderDoc Stock Blue Viewmodel Invis-Pass Finding
nodes.rationale: RenderDoc capture showed every stock viewmodel (pistol, right hand, left hand) is first drawn as transparent blue via ND-pass_invis.inc before its normal pass. Correction to an earlier assumption: a bad additive left hand looking blue is not material-ID corruption, it means the later normal/lit/fill/rim pass is missing, failing, or being dominated by this intentional first pass.

nodes.label: FunkMaxExport v0.6.0-customgroup Build
nodes.rationale: Added general build_custom_lgmd_bytes() core writer supporting multi-subobject mesh-group export with child/sibling hierarchy, named vhot_## helper export, rebuilt material tables, and a Package KPF button. LGMM/.CAL skeleton/weights and rotating PointRig joint authoring remained deferred; runtime AE proof was still pending at build time.

nodes.label: Native UI Draw-Range Scanner
nodes.rationale: Opt-in [ / ] hotkeys step individual native UI draw candidates. Proved the draw-number-to-panel mapping is not a fixed semantic ID list -- draw numbers shift by gameplay/inventory mode and equipped/carried items -- so final panel extraction must group by destination rect/bound texture/overlay slot, not draw ordinal.

nodes.label: Native Overlay Rect Rearrange Spike (Phase 2.8.1)
nodes.rationale: Spike rewrites gOverlayRects[50] to rearrange the 2D HUD (swap top/bottom bands) after validating the gOverlayOrder[50] signature. First pass captured the rect table too early and wrote from zero rects, collapsing icons to top-left; fixed by waiting for usable anchor rects (kOverlayInv/Ammo/Meters) before capture, then generalized to transform every usable rect by vertical band instead of a few named panels.

nodes.label: Right-Arm HUD Native-Rect Source Fix
nodes.rationale: The percentage-crop 'slice' method for the right-arm ammo hologram broke when inventory opened because the flat HUD graphic expanded and pulled in unrelated lower-right inventory/MFD data. Replaced with a native_rect mode that reads the validated gOverlayRects[50] ammo rect directly and fails closed (signature_mismatch/overlay_inactive/rect_invalid) instead of silently falling back to the known-bad slice.

nodes.label: SS2VR Triple Selection-Bracket System Confusion
nodes.rationale: Initially treated as one 'doubled bracket' bug. User correction clarified it was actually three separate systems: (1) unwanted SS2VR deep-world bracket on large non-interactable objects via a stale KEX objectUnderCursor fallback, (2) wanted SS2VR deep-world bracket on Squirrel-selected frobbable objects, and (3) the native flat 2D HUD bracket, misaligned in VR. Fixing (1) alone (dropping the objectUnderCursor fallback) then surfaced Squirrel highlight pollution (ss2vr_hl flicker) as the next-layer bug, stabilized with a hover latch.

nodes.label: SS2VR Selection Bracket Stereo-Eye Convergence Fix
nodes.rationale: Root cause of a remaining lagging duplicate bracket copy: the shared both-eyes bracket marker was computed from the post-stereo per-eye newView, so alternating eye offsets polluted a marker meant to be mono/stable. Fixed by computing the marker against the pre-eye-offset mono view (flatResidualView), falling back to newView only if unavailable.

nodes.label: Native Crosshair/Center-Frob Suppression
nodes.rationale: Adds suppress_native_crosshair/center_frob/brackets with a tracking-loss grace window: while controllers track, hides native overlay 22 and clears native object-under-cursor/hover/frob globals so objects can only be interacted with via controllers; falls back to native centre-crosshair frobbing if controller tracking is lost.

nodes.label: SS2VR Weapon Viewmodel HMD-Bleed Recurring Failure
nodes.rationale: Recurring failure mode across many builds (Phase 4.2.1, retested through v1.41-v1.43): the visible right-hand weapon model keeps reacting to HMD position/rotation instead of staying locked to the motion controller, despite projectile/world aim (pose_diag_right w*/dir fields) staying stable throughout. Roll-only compensation, disabling HMD rotational/positional compensation flags, and CameraObj translation remaps each reduced but did not fully eliminate the symptom; isolated to AE's CameraObj viewmodel-consumption path rather than the OpenXR pose bridge.

nodes.label: Headset UI Invisibility Fix (Force UI Quad Submission)
nodes.rationale: Inventory, gameplay HUD, and the main menu were invisible in headset (visible only on the desktop mirror) after enabling the right-arm HUD hologram path, because D3D only supplied a UI texture to OpenXR when submit_quad_layer, hand panel, or right-arm HUD were individually enabled. Fixed by passing uiFrameActive into OpenXR and always supplying the captured lastCandidateUiTexture_ so the full UI layer submits even with submit_quad_layer=false.

nodes.label: Gravity-Glove Held-Object Facing Axis-Order Fix
nodes.rationale: Grabbed/held objects moved correctly but their rotation did not match controller rotation, with pitch/bank feeling switched. Iterated through hold-facing modes (4, then 5) and heading/pitch sign knobs (ss2vr_phys_hold_heading_sign=-1) to align the applied Dark object-order (bank,pitch,heading) facing with controller orientation.

nodes.label: Snap-Turn Pixel-Per-Degree Gain Calibration
nodes.rationale: snap_turn_degrees=50 required about five right snaps to rotate 90 degrees, proving the pixel gain was under-rotating; a captured snap showed the route was effectively 1 pixel per degree while the config used snapPxPerDeg=1.40. Corrected the v1.49 default to snap_turn_pixels_per_degree=1.0 to match the observed KEX yaw-delta response.

nodes.label: Damage-Triggered Glitch FX Watcher
nodes.rationale: SS2VR.EffectHandler polls player HitPoints and on a drop sends a Debug.Command config trigger (ss2vr_fx glitch:<intensity>:<speed>) through the existing DLL config-setter hook/effect manager, reusing that hook as the only rendering path rather than adding a second FX system or native damage hook.
